overview: Research draft record, unpublished: every statement below is an unverified lead, not a verified fact. Кропивницький' and the vstup.osvita.ua 2025 admissions record name Kropyvnytskyi; the 2017 admissions record named Lyman, Donetsk oblast; Wikipedia says the university relocated from Donetsk to Kramatorsk in 2014), Ukraine, with leads for dentistry, medicine, pharmacy programmes. Draft record built from search-result leads on 2026-10-24; no official page was opened (official hosts are refused by this environment's network policy). The institution is reported as relocated; its current base is unconfirmed. No fee, deadline or intake date is recorded. Every field is awaiting verification against the official pages listed under research references, and nothing here is presented as a current fact.

Location lead as found (unverified): Kropyvnytskyi (reported current base, unverified: osvita.ua directory address 'вул. Юрія Коваленка, 4А, м. Кропивницький' and the vstup.osvita.ua 2025 admissions record name Kropyvnytskyi; the 2017 admissions record named Lyman, Donetsk oblast; Wikipedia says the university relocated from Donetsk to Kramatorsk in 2014)

Relocation lead (unverified): Leads only, chronology unverified. (1) Wikipedia: 'With the beginning of the Russo-Ukrainian Donbas war in 2014 the Donetsk National Medical University (DonNMU) relocated to Kramatorsk', with 'some faculty stayed in Russian-occupied Donetsk, where a separate university is recognized only by Russia'. (2) vstup.osvita.ua 2017 record names Lyman (Donetsk oblast); a Lyman Medical Professional College is described as a separate structural unit of DNMU (education.ua/colleges/400; regulation PDF approved 2017). (3) Suspilne Kropyvnytskyi (undated in snippet): students collected signatures against closure of the Kropyvnytskyi branch; the acting rector said the branch would close at the end of June and the material base would be moved to Kramatorsk. (4) Suspilne (undated in snippet, article 257050): 'Обладнання медичного університету на 30 мільйонів гривень вивезли з Краматорська до Кропивницького' and about half a thousand DNMU graduates received diplomas in Kropyvnytskyi. (5) Suspilne (article 230671, undated in snippet): the DNMU surgery department works in Haivoron hospital, Kirovohrad oblast, with salaries paid by the university. (6) Current directories (osvita.ua guide; vstup.osvita.ua 2025) give Kropyvnytskyi as the address/settlement, and the university published a 2024 enrolment protocol, a Feb 2023 booklet and a 2023 Prozorro tender, so it appears to be operating as a relocated institution; the registered legal address and the actual teaching base(s) in 2025/26 are unverified.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Name confusion with the occupation-side institution in Donetsk ('Donetsk National Medical University named after M. Gorky', inventory slug donetsk-gorky-occupied), which Wikipedia describes as 'recognized only by Russia'; aggregator pages and old 'M. Gorky' naming may mix the two. Any profile must state that the Ukrainian DNMU is the relocated, Ministry-supervised institution and never link to occupation-side hosts.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Base unsettled: Kropyvnytskyi (current directory address), Kramatorsk (2014 relocation; front-line city) and Lyman (2017 record; college site) all appear in results; dates of the moves are not shown in the snippets. Undated Suspilne reports describe a dispute over closing the Kropyvnytskyi branch (acting rector planned to move the base to Kramatorsk) that conflicts with later leads showing Kropyvnytskyi as the main base.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Governance lead: the search summary mentioned a report that the Ministry was preparing a decision to suspend rector Kondratenko; the source URL and date could not be pinned down in the result set - unverified, do not publish.
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Domain confusion: Ukrainian directories and the university's own PDFs use dnmu.edu.ua, while Indian aggregators cite dnmu.com.ua.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Aggregator claims (WHO/GMC/NMC recognition, USD 3,700-5,300 fees, NEET requirement, Feb/Sept intakes, '2000+ international students a year', 'Admission 2026-27') are self-reported and unverified; they must not be reused as facts.
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Conflicting student numbers (about 4,200 on the Study in Ukraine portal vs over 10,000 and 15,200 on other sites).

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Lyman Medical Professional College of DNMU (education.ua/colleges/400) is a vocational 'фаховий коледж' structural unit, not the university; it must not be listed as a degree provider.
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: An Ombudsman (ombudsman.gov.ua) PDF titled 'Звіт Донецький' appeared in the results; its subject and content are unknown.
